title: Ledger anchoring for progressive streaming credits and adaptive throttles
creator: Evan Morales
description:
Problem: Streaming sessions that emit partial fragments (progressive outputs) are causing inconsistent token ledgers when combined with mid-stream model switches, dynamic throttles, and client reconnects. In several customer incidents we observed: (1) duplicate crediting when partial fragments are re-sent after reconnect, (2) under-crediting when preempted fragments are dropped by fallback routing, and (3) misattribution between input (prompt) and generated output tokens across multipart/noncanonical frames. This ticket implements a ledger anchoring mechanism plus an adaptive crediting protocol to make progressive streaming metering deterministic and robust to reconnects, backpressure, and model handoffs.

Scope: implement server-side ledger anchors per-session with idempotent fragment attribution; integrate anchors with the rate-limiter to ensure provisional credits can be rolled forward or rolled back deterministically; add a reconciliation job (fast-path) that runs on reconnect to compact provisional anchors and finalize credits. Changes span: streaming ingress middleware, metering pipeline, rate-limiter interaction, and billing finalizer service.

Goals: produce deterministic token tallies even under out-of-order frames, transient reconnects, and mid-session model variant switches; keep tail latency and throughput within current SLOs; provide transparent audit traces for customer support and billing disputes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end test harness reproduces reconnect + duplicate-fragment scenario and results in identical final token ledger between baseline deterministic run and production run with anchors enabled.
2) No increase in p95 tail latency for 90% of testcases (measured on staging perf harness).
3) Billing finalizer records atomic anchor transitions and emits auditable delta events for any rollbacks (log format validated).

4) Rate-limiter honors provisional credits: clients are not prematurely throttled for already-provisioned tokens and provisional credits are reconciled within 30s after session finalization or reconnect.
5) Integration smoke tests for model handoff during active stream show no double-credit events across 1000 randomized handoffs.
implementation_notes: High-level approach: (a) allocate a monotonically increasing session anchor token (UUID + seq) at stream start; (b) each emitted fragment references the anchor and local offset; (c) metering pipeline records fragments as provisional credits keyed by anchor+offset; (d) on final terminal frame (or explicit finalize), provisional credits are atomically promoted to committed credits; (e) on reconnect, the client provides last-observed anchor+offset and server reconciles by idempotently ignoring already-committed offsets and reapplying missing ones. Interplay with throttling: rate-limiter tracks provisional credit windows and allows a graceful temporary buffer of N provisional tokens per session; when provisional budget is exhausted, streaming is backpressured. To avoid permanent leakage, provisional credits have TTL and the finalizer will roll back expired provisionals with a compensating event.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: We evaluated two alternatives: (1) client-driven checkpoints where clients must ack tokens to commit; (2) purely stateless dedupe using content hashes. Client-driven checkpoints places too much burden on SDKs and increases latency; stateless dedupe fails for semantically identical but byte-different partials and cannot handle mid-model handoff reliably. Ledger anchoring centralizes correctness at the server with modest state cost (per-active-session anchor metadata ~200 bytes). Concern: additional memory in peak load; mitigations include eager eviction of low-activity anchors and batching finalizer work.
tests: Unit tests for anchor allocation, provisional -> committed transition, and rollback. End-to-end simulated harness that runs randomized sequences: small fragments, large fragments, reconnect with replay, mid-session model swap, and injected network duplicates. Load test on staging with 5k concurrent streaming sessions for 1 hour measuring p50/p95/p99 latencies and memory footprint. Fraud detection test: simulate a client that rapidly reopens sessions to try to duplicate credits — ensure rate-limiter backpressure and finalizer rollbacks prevent revenue leakage.
deployment_plan: 1) Feature flagged rollout in staging for internal validation. 2) Canary rollout to 10% of streaming traffic in us-west1 with detailed audit log sampling. 3) Monitor billing delta, p95 latency, memory usage, and reconciliation failure rate; hold if reconciliation failures exceed 0.1% or billing delta > 0.05%. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% over two weeks with live customer support on standby. 5) Post-rollout 7-day audit comparing new ledger totals vs legacy bucket for a sample of accounts.
comments: 2026-02-15 Evan Morales: Triage complete — incident analysis points to three recurring failure modes when streams are preempted and retried. Risk of customer disputes if not addressed before next high-volume release.
2026-02-20 Priya Natarajan: Design PR created (link in design_links). Chose server-anchored approach to avoid SDK churn. Initial proto implemented in serving/streaming-middleware branch.
2026-02-26 Reviewer (Diego Ramos): Asked for stronger invariants on finalizer idempotency; suggested storing commit tombstones for 24 hours to guard against clock skew and late replays.

2026-03-02 QA (Lina Park): Added e2e harness cases for randomized model handoffs; discovered a starvation scenario when provisional budget is shared across multiplexed sessions — flagged for follow-up (ENG-882470).

2026-03-07 Priya Natarajan: Implemented tombstone window and per-session provisional cap. Memory estimates updated: +0.5GB at 5k concurrent streams. Added rollback audit events to billing pipeline. PRs opened.

2026-03-10 Evan Morales: Load test run finished. p95 latency within target; observed 0.02% reconciliation errors due to rare DB transient — added exponential retry and circuit-breaker in finalizer. Ready for canary pending security review.
2026-03-10 Security (Anya Feldman): Requested threat model for anchor replay attack and confirmation that HMAC of session token + anchor is validated. Action: security review in progress.
2026-03-10 Support (Rajiv Gupta): Prepared customer-facing notes and dashboard panels for dispute triage.
